# Synapse 2.0.12

Synapse AI asks before it guesses and says what it assumed, a new request typed beside an open workflow is built as new, and Home never says nothing is waiting before it knows.

## Changed

- **Synapse AI asks what it can't know, at most twice, and says what it assumed.** When a request leaves something only you can say, such as which terms a document is checked against, Synapse AI asks, in no more than two rounds of questions. Past that it builds, and the plan card lists what it assumed under **What I assumed**. Every card now says **How it starts** (a form, a schedule, or by hand), and a part of your request that only one branch of the workflow would do is called out.
- **A new request typed beside an open workflow is built as new.** When a workflow is open and you describe a different job, Synapse AI builds it as a new workflow instead of reading it as a change to the open one. When it can't tell, it asks once whether you mean a change or something new. "Run it" right after a request that built nothing now says so and offers to build it.
- **No stronger model is suggested before a build unless it is measured to be better.** Synapse AI used to suggest a bigger model before many builds, even when you had picked your model yourself. It no longer does. When it offers to try again on a stronger model after a failure, it names both models by their names.
- **Saving to your workspace's own Vault needs no approval step.** A plan that writes to the Vault no longer needs a person to approve that step first. Sending email, posting to Slack, calling outside services and your own custom tools still ask first, as before.
- **A model CLI that is signed out is no longer offered.** When Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex or GitHub Copilot's CLI is installed but not signed in, the model pickers leave its models out. A model you already saved on it stays visible where it is set.

## Fixed

- **The OpenAI Agent Builder import asks for the export.** Sending the import line with nothing pasted under it no longer builds a guess. The panel holds the line back and says where the export comes from (in Agent Builder: Code → Agents SDK), in a note you can read in full.
- **Synapse AI explains what it can build instead of a dead end.** When a very long request left Synapse AI's planner answering in prose, the turn could end with "I couldn't turn that into something I can make or change here." It now explains what can be built here and offers choices.
- **Home never says nothing is waiting before it knows.** While Home was still loading, or when something couldn't be read, it could say "Nothing is waiting on you.", "No runs yet" or "Nothing runs on its own yet." Each part of Home now waits for what it reads, and if something can't be read, Home says so, with **Try again**, instead of showing an empty list or a zero.

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.12`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.0.x:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.
